blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Can response safety be scored by cosine similarity to the mean embedding of known-safe
responses? A recent sleeper-agent detector proposes exactly this score, yet the raw
positive-centroid rule is not identified: positive observations locate the safe class
relative to an encoder origin, but do not determine which direction separates safe from
unsafe responses. We audit the rule on two prompt-controlled, human-labeled corpora and
one auxiliary jury-labeled source control, using four frozen encoders and prompt-grouped
splits. On the human-labeled corpora the safe prototype reaches ROC-AUC 0.457–0.545,
with two cells significantly below chance and one above, while an explicit
safe-minus-unsafe reference reaches 0.588–0.738 on the same embeddings; on the jury
control the prototype is inverted (0.358–0.405) and the reference reaches 0.754–0.793.
At validation-calibrated 5% false-safe thresholds, the reference accepts more safe
responses on PKU-SafeRLHF (0.153–0.263 versus
0.039–0.061 across encoders) and Aegis (0.189–0.291
versus 0.004–0.045), but not reliably on BeaverTails. A fully unlabeled
held-out reference recovers part to most of the referenced ranking, much less when only
5% of the pool is unsafe, whereas 80–634 labeled unsafe responses
recover most of it. Prompt-only ablations show that prompt-label composition can inflate uncontrolled
evaluations. This is a bounded result about a raw positive centroid, not all one-class
methods or safety-specialized guards. A class mean is a location, not necessarily a
safety direction; a declared reference with enough unsafe mass identifies orientation.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
A single prototype is an appealing safety readout. Given embeddings of responses
labeled safe, average and normalize them, then score a candidate by cosine similarity.
The rule is transparent, cheap, and appears to need labels from only one class. That
last property is attractive when unsafe examples are sensitive, incomplete, or costly
to curate. The rule has also been proposed as a detector score: a recent sleeper-agent
detector flags a response when one minus its cosine similarity to a centroid of
safe-mode responses, embedded with all-MiniLM-L6-v2 (one of the four encoders we
audit), is high, OR-combining this signal with a canary-question check ( Zanbaghi et al., 2025 ) .
Its triggered responses are topically distinct from the safe ones, the easy case for a
location score; our audit holds topic fixed.

blocks.en:
The shortcut hides a measurement problem. A class mean is a location relative to the
encoder origin; a class-separating direction is a displacement relative to another
distribution. Those are different objects. In a shifted or concentrated embedding
space, unsafe responses can project more strongly onto the normalized safe mean than
safe responses do (Figure 1 ). A score called “similarity to safe”
can then rank unsafe responses higher without any reversal of semantic meaning.

This matters for language-model security, where moderators err in two directions,
accepting unsafe compliance and rejecting benign responses, and a high aggregate AUC may
reflect prompt composition rather than response behavior. We ask four falsifiable
questions: (i) is the positive prototype’s
orientation identified from safe examples alone, (ii) does an explicit reference
improve ranking under prompt or label-source controls, (iii) does that improvement
survive validation-calibrated false-safe constraints, and (iv) can an unlabeled
reference replace unsafe labels in finite samples?

blocks.en:
We answer with a provenance-audited study on BeaverTails ( Ji et al., 2023 ) ,
PKU-SafeRLHF ( Ji et al., 2025 ) , and Aegis 2.0 ( Ghosh et al., 2025 ) . The first two primary
arms use human-released safety labels and prompt-matched comparisons; Aegis is
explicitly an auxiliary llm_jury -only source control. Four frozen encoders
cover two sentence-transformer models and mean-pooled hidden states from two sizes of
Qwen2.5-Instruct ( Reimers and Gurevych, 2019 ; Qwen Team, 2025 ) . Exact prompt grouping, deduplication,
source controls, response-overlap sensitivity, and cluster bootstrap intervals address
the leakage and provenance defects that commonly make safety-evaluation conclusions
fragile.

blocks.en:
Our contributions are: 1. We formalize positive-only non-identification: the same safe embedding
distribution is compatible with unsafe distributions that induce opposite signs
for the prototype’s expected score gap. 2. We show a controlled empirical pattern across 12 corpus–encoder cells with
family-wise inference. The raw safe prototype is weak on the human-labeled corpora
(AUC 0.457–0.545) and inverted on the jury control (0.358–0.405); 7
of 12 cells differ from chance after Holm correction, 6 of them below. It
never outranks a response-length heuristic by more than 0.016 and
falls below a 12-feature stylistic baseline in every cell. A difference-of-means
reference is above chance everywhere (0.588–0.738 human-labeled; 0.754–0.793
jury). 3. At validation-calibrated 5% and 10% false-safe targets, referencing raises
safe acceptance on PKU-SafeRLHF and Aegis for every encoder; on BeaverTails the gain
is small and uncertain. 4. We separate prompt-disjointness from prompt control: prompt-only prediction
falls to near chance on matched cohorts even when it is strong on full corpus
populations. 5. We test label-free orientation out of sample. A fully unlabeled held-out
reference recovers part to most of the referenced ranking, little at 5% unsafe
prevalence, while a small labeled unsafe set from other prompts recovers most of it.

blocks.en:
The scope is deliberately narrow. That orientation needs a reference is a standard
lesson of one-class and positive–unlabeled learning (Section 2 ). What
is missing for response safety is a measurement of how the unreferenced rule behaves on
real safety data once prompt composition is controlled, what it costs at an operating
point, and how much a label-free reference recovers in finite samples. We do not claim
that all one-class estimators fail, that these scores are deployable guards, or that
Aegis jury labels constitute a human replication.

blocks.en: 2 Related work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en:
Representation-level directions are used to analyze and steer refusal behavior ( Arditi et al., 2024 ) . Concurrent RankOne work forms per-prompt safe-minus-unsafe
directions and studies their transfer ( Anonymous ACL ARR submission, 2026 ) , and multi-layer prototype
moderation scores inputs by Gaussian (Mahalanobis) distance to safe and unsafe class
prototypes in hidden states ( Chrabąszcz et al., 2025 ) ; both are referenced readouts in
our terms. Our object is
the positive endpoint alone. We include global difference-of-means, two-centroid,
RankOne, and supervised linear readouts to distinguish an unreferenced-location failure
from a failure of linear or global readouts. We do not compete with instruction-tuned
guards such as Llama Guard and ShieldGemma ( Inan et al., 2023 ; Zeng et al., 2024 ) , or with safety-specialized sentence
encoders ( Kim et al., 2024 ) .

blocks.en:
The sleeper-agent detector above scores response drift as one minus cosine similarity to
a safe-response centroid ( Zanbaghi et al., 2025 ) . Embedding-drift monitoring can
compare a production batch mean with a reference batch mean, which declares both
endpoints ( Filippova and Samuylova, 2023 ; Arize AI, 2026 ) . Closer to density
estimation, recent alignment-failure monitors fit a Gaussian to hidden states of safe
conversations and score Mahalanobis distance ( Feng et al., 2026 ) . For vision–language
jailbreaks, benign-cluster Mahalanobis baselines are strong, yet the same work argues
that one-class designs over-reject unseen benign inputs and proposes contrastive scores
that model both classes ( Hua et al., 2025 ) . Those methods estimate covariance and
support; our claim concerns cosine to a single mean and does not extend to them.

blocks.en:
Figure 2 gives the central result. Across the two human-labeled,
prompt-controlled corpora, the safe prototype is weak rather than uniformly at chance:
AUC spans 0.457–0.545. Holm–Bonferroni over the 12 prototype-versus-chance tests
rejects 7: 6 below chance (all four Aegis cells, and PKU-SafeRLHF
mpnet and Qwen-3B) and 1 above (BeaverTails Qwen-0.5B). The pronounced
inversion is confined to the auxiliary Aegis jury control (0.358–0.405); the two
significant PKU-SafeRLHF cells have point estimates within 0.05 of chance, and
4 cells are formally equivalent to chance at that margin
(Appendix Table 5 ). Difference-of-means is above chance in every cell:
0.588–0.622 on BeaverTails, 0.668–0.738 on PKU-SafeRLHF, and 0.754–0.793 on Aegis.
The same frozen embeddings therefore contain separable signal; what fails is treating
an unreferenced positive location as an oriented axis.

blocks.en: 6 Implications for language-model security

blocks.en:
“Similarity to safe” is not coordinate-free. A security readout should state
the negative or unlabeled distribution that orients it, and an unlabeled reference must
hold enough unsafe mass to survive sampling shift.

blocks.en:
Above-chance AUC is not a deployment threshold; false-safe constraints expose how much
benign traffic a detector rejects. Even the referenced direction accepts at most
0.095 of safe BeaverTails responses at its 5% target, so these readouts are
diagnostics, not filters.

A one-class readout should be compared with response length and simple stylistic
features before it is called a safety score. Inverting the prototype would improve AUC in some cells, but the required
sign is corpus-dependent and would be selected after viewing test labels. A declared
reference, not post-hoc sign choice, identifies orientation.

blocks.en: 7 Limitations and broader impact
blocks.zh: 7. 限制和更广泛的影响

blocks.en:
Our conclusion concerns a raw positive centroid scored by cosine. It does not rule out
support estimators, Gaussian or other density models, positive–unlabeled methods,
safety-specialized encoders, or supervised guards. The study covers English responses,
two SBERT-family encoders, and one Qwen family at two scales under fixed pooling and
truncation; category-conditional performance and truncation by label are not audited.
BeaverTails and
PKU-SafeRLHF use released human annotations without a new adjudication study. Aegis is
jury-only in our primary arm and is auxiliary evidence. Only the population reference
in Section 5.4 is built without labels: the cohort pools for BeaverTails
and PKU-SafeRLHF are selected by label (mixed-label prompts or discordant pairs), and
the 5%, 10%, and 25% pools are subsampled by label; only their means enter the score.
The stylistic baseline covers simple surface features, not all style.

Bootstrap intervals hold the train-fitted direction fixed. They quantify test sampling
and, for operating points, validation-threshold variability, but omit train-refit
uncertainty. Thresholds are calibrated separately per corpus and method; they are not
portable deployment thresholds. The 5% and 10% targets are diagnostic and remain
too permissive for many high-stakes uses. We measure ranking and acceptance errors, not
changes in model behavior, attack robustness, or real-world harm.

blocks.en: 8 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 8 结论

blocks.en:
Positive examples identify where a safe class lies, not which way safety increases.
Across controlled cohorts and four encoders, a raw safe centroid is weak or inverted and
below simple stylistic features, while an explicit reference improves ranking and, on two
of three corpora, calibrated safe acceptance; an unlabeled reference helps only to the
extent that it carries unsafe mass. Declare the reference, control prompt composition, compare
with nuisance baselines, and evaluate a held-out operating point before calling an
embedding score a safety direction.
